clusters.state_of_play: A Chinese state-linked hacking campaign, attributed to Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology Company, breached numerous US government agencies including the Federal Reserve, Senate, NASA, DOJ, Energy, HHS and NIH, plus defense, healthcare, power, telecom, and financial sectors; the FBI has seized domains and disrupted botnet infrastructure, while a separate probe into hacks on US water systems and PLCs across Minnesota and other states is expanding. Separately, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish keynote at Jackson Hole warning that inflation progress is insufficient and the Fed 'may have work to do,' prompting investors to raise bets on a rate hike (including a possible September move), a jump in the 2-year Treasury yield, and mixed analyst reaction contrasting his clearer stance with a confusing July press conference. Commentary now frames Warsh's stance as risking a political clash with Trump, who favors lower rates, ahead of the midterms, while inflation pressures are also linked to the six-month mark of Trump's Iran war and a tariff dispute with Canada.

clusters.state_of_play: Iceland's referendum on resuming EU membership talks has concluded: the 'No' campaign prevailed with about 52.8% of votes to 47.2% for 'Yes', overturning the early lead for 'Yes'. The count, confirmed as official, saw record turnout and swung back and forth overnight. Coverage links the outcome to Donald Trump's threats to annex Greenland and concerns over fishing rights; Reykjavik was the only region to record a 'Yes' majority. Iceland remains part of the EEA and Schengen area despite the rejection.
